hints: Look at Imani's and Zeke's statements. Neither is about the gulls, so whose word is each one backing?
Imani's statement stands or falls with Carmen's, and Zeke's with Basil's. Exactly four true means just one statement is false.
A false statement from Carmen, Imani, Basil or Zeke would bring a second one with it. So the one false statement is Otis's.

solution.key_idea: Imani backs Carmen and Zeke backs Basil, so a false statement among those four would come in a pair; the single false one is Otis's.
steps: Exactly four true statements means exactly one is false.
Imani says Carmen is truthful, so their statements are both true or both false. Zeke and Basil are tied the same way.
A false statement from any of those four would bring a second with it. So Otis's statement is the only false one.
Otis is wrong, so neither Imani nor Zeke fed the gulls. Basil is right, so neither Otis nor Imani did.
Carmen is right, so Basil did not. That leaves Carmen herself.
Check Carmen: every statement but Otis's is true, which makes exactly four. So Carmen fits.
solution.epilogue: Carmen had tossed her stale popcorn off the pier for the fish, she said. The gulls got there first, and she spent the rest of the cook-off shooing them from the tasting tables.
